classTitle: Emissions, global warming potentials and the global carbon cycle

body:
1. Understand the categories & tools for energy modeling in climate tech
2. Produce results from an energy modeling tool

Read through at least one of these. Here's what we recommend, in rough priority order:
  • Read pages 29-33 in Fighting Words: JP Morgan's 16th Annual Energy Paper (published March 3, 2026, so this is brand new). This section covers the "primary energy fallacy" and what electrification really means for the energy system.
    • Consider that decarbonizing our power supply has two steps:
      • Electrify everything: replace direct fossil fuel use with electricity wherever possible
      • Decarbonize the grid: make electricity generation 100% clean
    • Both of these are highly complex and nuanced issues with lots of impact opportunities. Modeling is a critical part of this!
    • Then skim pages 65-68 (Essential Charts) for the big picture on renewable energy and electrification by country.
  • Read About Building Energy Modeling (DOE) for an introduction to what building energy modeling is, how it's used, and the open-source tools (EnergyPlus, OpenStudio) behind it.
  • Listen to a Volts podcast on grid infrastructure (pick one):
    • What's the deal with interconnection queues? (~50 min, 2023) explains why it takes 3-5 years for renewable projects to connect to the grid
    • Can data centers be good grid citizens? (~52 min, 2025) looks at how data center demand is straining the grid and what flexible design can do about it
  • Explore Berkeley Lab's "Queued Up" interactive data to see the 10,300+ projects currently waiting in US interconnection queues.
